			<a name="Business"></a><font style="display: inline;">Item 1.&nbsp;&nbsp;Business.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Lumos Networks Corp. Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Lumos Networks Corp. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">(&#x201C;Lumos Networks,&#x201D; the &#x201C;Company,&#x201D; &#x201C;we,&#x201D; &#x201C;us&#x201D; or &#x201C;our&#x201D;) </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">is</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">a fiber-based </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">bandwidth infrastructure and service provider</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> in the Mid-Atlantic region.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">We provide services to carrier and enterprise customers, including healthcare providers, local government agencies, financial institutions, educational institutions, and other enterprises over our approximately 8,600 route-mile fiber network.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our principal products and services include Multiprotocol Label Switching (&#x201C;MPLS&#x201D;) based Ethernet, Metro Ethernet (&#x201C;Metro E&#x201D;), Fiber to the Cell site (&#x201C;FTTC&#x201D;) wireless backhaul and data transport services, wavelength transport services and IP services.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">We </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">became an independent, publicly traded company</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> on October 31, 2011,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> as a result of our spin-off from NTELOS Holdings Corp. (&#x201C;NTELOS&#x201D;).&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">O</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">ur common stock</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> has been</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> publicly trade</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">d</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> on The NASDAQ Stock Market LLC (&#x201C;NASDAQ&#x201D;) u</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">nder the ticker symbol &#x201C;LMOS</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> since November 1, 2011.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">We conduct all of our business through our wholly-owned subsidiary Lumos Networks Operating Company and its subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our principal executive offices are located at One Lumos Plaza, Waynesboro, Virginia 22980.&nbsp;&nbsp;The telephone number at that address is (540) 946-2000.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Business Strategy</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our </font><font style="display: inline;">overall</font><font style="display: inline;"> strategy is to transition into a pure-play fiber bandwidth infrastructure company through pursuit of expansion opportunities, both organic and inorganic. To achieve organic growth, our objective is to leverage and expand our fiber assets to capture the growing demand for data and mobility services among our carrier and enterprise customers in our marketplace. Our </font><font style="display: inline;">operating </font><font style="display: inline;">strategy is to (i) leverage our fiber network to expand to new fiber to the cell opportunities; (ii) monetize our approximately 8,600 route-mile fiber optic network by selling bandwidth infrastructure services to new and existing carrier and enterprise customers while maintaining a ratio of approximately 80% of our data revenue from on-net traffic;&nbsp; (iii) use our </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">expansion</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;"> and "edge-out&#x201D; strategies to expand into new markets and markets adjacent to our existing footprint to </font><font style="display: inline;">increase </font><font style="display: inline;">our addressable market size; (iv) proactively manage our churn through several initiatives including upgrading existing customers from legacy technologies to carrier Ethernet services and continually improving network a</font><font style="display: inline;">nd operational performance; </font><font style="display: inline;">(v) focus on managing resources from the declining legacy voice products into our faster growing and more profitable data products;</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> (vi) execute our success-based investment strategy to maintain our capital efficiency and expand margins. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Our data segment, which provided approximately 56% of our total revenue in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, represents the main growth opportunity and is the key focal point of our strategy and includes our enterprise data, transport and FTTC product groups</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Given our focus on on-net customers, our data services typically carry higher gross margins than many of our other services.&nbsp;&nbsp;A significant majority of our capital expenditures and sales force are dedicated to increasing revenue and profit from our data segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that a balanced split between enterprise and carrier revenue results in the most effective capital allocation and resulting profitability.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are focused on taking advantage of increased carrier bandwidth demand, p</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">articularly for long-term </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">FTTC </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">contracts from wireless carriers that are deploying </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">long-term evolution (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">LTE</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> data services, selling into our expansion and edge-out</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> markets, maximizing the use of our carrier end user distribution channel, connecting our enterprise customers to data centers and improving penetration in existing markets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Our residential and small business (&#x201C;R&amp;SB&#x201D;) and RLEC access segments provided approximately 33% and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">11%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> of our total revenue in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our R&amp;SB segment includes legacy voice and IP service</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> products targeted to our residential and small business customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our RLEC access segment provides other carriers access to our network within our RLEC territories, primarily </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">through switched access services.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Th</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">ese </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">segment</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> require limited incremental capital to maintain the underlying assets and deliver reasonably predictable cash flows.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Despite declining revenues as a result of regulatory actions taken to reduce intra-state tariffs, access line loss resulting from residential wireless substitution, technology changes and product replacement of voice service offerings from cable operators in our markets,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> we expect the cash flows from these legacy businesses to continue to significantly contribute to funding the capital investment in our growing data segment. &nbsp;Alternatively, we could explore the separation of these assets in order to monetize them </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">more expediently </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">through a sale or some other transaction. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">The </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">key imperatives for our data growth initiatives are as follows</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Enhance </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Carrier Ethernet Network and</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> Grow FTTC Revenues</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">As demand for FTTC services, gr</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">eater data transport bandwidth </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">and guaranteed network stability continues, there is an increasing demand to provide carrier </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Ethernet</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> networks to our wireless carrier customers and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">select </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">large data transport </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">customers. In 2014, we completed the core constructio</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">n of an approximately 850-mile</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> carrier network within our existing fiber network to provide FTTC solutions to multiple large wireless communication providers</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> and select large enterprise customers</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> who operate in our markets</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">connected the first FTTC sites to this carrier network</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">. This migration continued through 2015 and we expect to have</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> substantially all</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">existing </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">FTTC traffic transitioned early in 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">. Additionally, new traffic has been and will continue to be added directly to this network</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font provided </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">FTTC connectivity to 1,099</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> cell sites.&nbsp;&nbsp;We </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">intend to significantly increase</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> FTTC connectivity to cell sites </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New 			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Enhance Legacy Enterprise Networks and Grow Enterprise Revenues</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">As demand for greater data bandwidth and guaranteed network stability continues to grow within </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">e</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">nterprise services, we continue to invest capital in expanding and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">enhancing</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> our enterprise networks to accommodate our customer needs. Growing our enterprise revenues using a success-based expansion </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">approach is critical to e</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">nsuring the desired returns on invested capital are met.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">, our </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">8,600</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> route-mile fiber network was connected to approximately 1,732 buildings.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">We believe there is significant </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">prospect </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">to compete for opportunities to connect to additional buildings and data centers in close proximity to our existing fiber network.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our primary sales channels are enterprise-direct and carrier end user.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our carrier end user channel facilitates the sale of enterprise data </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">services </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">for national carrier customers that are within our footprint.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Through use of this sales channel we are able to leverage </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">our existing fiber infrastructure to grow revenue and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">reduce </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">the likelihood of being overbuilt within our markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to our initiatives centered on enhancing our network and improving operational performance, we will continue to deliberately and proactively manage our </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">enterprise </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">customers </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">with </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">legacy services to our Ethernet</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">-based</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> services, and appropriately incent our sales force to focus on renewal of long-term contracts with the intent of reducing churn and improving the customer experience</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Driven by demand from existing enterprise and carrier customers</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> our e</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">xpansion</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> strategy </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">grows</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> our fiber network into new contiguous markets by leveraging existing and new assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our current e</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">xpansion </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">markets are Richmond, VA and Norfolk, VA (including t</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">he nearby C</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">ity of Petersburg and the Hampton Roads area).&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">In </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">, we added 785 route miles </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">of new fiber to our network, which </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">includes our </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">partially completed </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">fiber network expansion </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">822</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> route miles in the Richmond and Norfolk area. As we </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">expand </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">into these new markets we are </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">significantly increasing our addressable market size, thus allowing us </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">to bring new FTTC carrier customers and enterprise customers onto our fiber networks</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Our edge-o</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">ut strategy, which focuses on </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">incrementally adding network assets and new customers in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">markets </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">in close proximity </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">to our existing footprint</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> is complementary to our expansion strategy in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">the Richmond, VA and Norfolk, VA</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> area</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Drive Incremental On-</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Net Data Traffic</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Our on-net strategy focuses on driving traffic through our network, thereby increasing profitability.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> As our network footprint grows and the bandwidth demand increases, we are able to drive incremental revenue through our existing network with minimal increase in operating expenses or incremental capital expenditures.&nbsp;&nbsp;We evaluate this on-net approach and the associated capital expenditure against the revenue opportunity and have determined that maintaining approximately 80% of our data revenue from on-net traffic is the most effective use of capital.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Use </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Disciplined</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> Success-Based Capital Investment Strategy</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">We seek to maximize our capital expenditure efficiency by requiring that a significant percentage of our capital investment be tied to specific revenue generating products based on customer commitments, which we refer to as &#x201C;success-based projects&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our success-based capital investment strategy involves maximizing capital expenditure efficiency by pursuing on-net and near-net customer </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Business Segments</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">We have three reportable business segments, as follows:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 36pt 6pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Data&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our data segment includes our enterprise data, transport and FTTC product groups.&nbsp;&nbsp;We market and sell these services primarily to carriers and enterprise customers, including healthcare providers, state and local government agencies, financial institutions, and educational institutions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues from our data segment accounted for 56.0%, </font><font style="display: inline;">52.9%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">50.2%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of our total revenue for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Data product lines are growing at a pace that significantly exceeds our legacy product lines and in aggregate, they also provide a higher gross margin.&nbsp;&nbsp;The objective of our data segment is to leverage the ever increasing data bandwidth demands from our enterprise and carrier customers in our existing and expanding addressable markets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our data segment operations are based upon our </font><font style="display: inline;">expansion, </font><font style="display: inline;">edge-out and on-net strategies that seek to </font><font style="display: inline;">capitalize on </font><font style="display: inline;">new markets by maximizing the use of our fiber assets while optimizing capital efficiency and profitability.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2015, we continued to re-deploy capital and personnel resources away from our declining legacy product lines towards our growth businesses within our data segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our strategy requires disciplined use of capital expenditures on success-based projects to grow our fiber assets and reach an increasing number of both carrier and enterprise customers. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In addition to the higher gross margins that are characteristic of the data business and our on-net expansion, we have also been able to deliver other enterprise services, such as metro Ethernet transport as a direct result of our expanding network.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe our </font><font style="display: inline;">expansion, edge-out and </font><font style="display: inline;">on-net strategies, combined with our commitment to customer service, will continue to attract larger customers in our key vertical markets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We generate growth within our data segment </font><font style="display: inline;">through </font><font style="display: inline;">new </font><font style="display: inline;">long-term FTTC contracts </font><font style="display: inline;">with </font><font style="display: inline;">wireless carriers deploying LTE</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">services</font><font style="display: inline;"> and bandwidth upgrades on existing contracts</font><font style="display: inline;">, improving enterprise penetration within our existing and </font><font style="display: inline;">new </font><font style="display: inline;">markets and providing greater Ethernet bandwidth to enterprise customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, we added 241 FTTC sites, representing a year-over-year increase of approximately 28.1%, and 255 on-net buildings, representing an increase of approximately 17.3% year-over-year.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our sales force is organized into carrier and enterprise teams to effectively pursue the </font><font style="display: inline;">respective </font><font style="display: inline;">opportunities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our ability to sustain or accelerate revenue growth in our data segment depends on our ability to obtain and effectively deploy capital to upgrade and expand our fiber network and implement our FTTC and edge-out plans in a timely and disciplined manner, attract new customers and successfully manage churn downwards thro</font><font style="display: inline;">ugh customer retention programs, including </font><font style="display: inline;">upgrading existing customers from legacy technologies to carrier Ethernet services. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 36pt 6pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">R&amp;SB</font>

</font><font style="display: inline;">data segment</font><font style="display: inline;">) and the following IP services products: fiber-to-the-premise broadband XL, DSL, integrated access and </font><font style="display: inline;">IPTV </font><font style="display: inline;">video</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;These products are sold to </font><font style="display: inline;">residential and small business</font><font style="display: inline;"> customers through our competitive local exchange carrier (&#x201C;CLEC&#x201D;) and rural local exchange carrier (&#x201C;RLEC&#x201D;) network</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues from our </font><font style="display: inline;">R&amp;SB</font><font 			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Sales.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">We serve our carrier and enterprise customers with our suite of fiber-based data products, which include carrier Ethernet, MPLS, VPN, wavelength and dedicated Internet access.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have continued to see increased demand for these products across our customer base, particularly as demand for data transport and mobility services grow.&nbsp;&nbsp;The mission of our sales team is to capitalize on this growing demand by offering customized solutions to our carrier and enterprise customers with a continued focus on expanding within our key vertical markets, which include healthcare, education, financial services and government.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our technical team plays a significant role in our sales approach in order to focus on selling customized, long-term and secure networking and data solutions.&nbsp; </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Our Network and Platform</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">We have developed a fiber optic network of long-haul fiber, carrier Ethernet and Ethernet rings located primarily in Virginia and West Virginia, and portions of Pennsylvania, Maryland, Ohio and Kentucky.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2015, our fiber network spanned approximately 8,600 route miles.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">Our integrated fiber transport network allows us to offer a suite of advanced next-generation communications services, including, but not limited to, 100Gbps wavelength services, which provides greater throughput and superior latency performance, multi-site networking, dedicated Internet and MEF 2.0 certified Ethernet solutions, high-speed Internet and VoIP services.&nbsp;&nbsp;We use a multi-vendor approach, including Cisco, Alcatel-Lucent and Ciena, among others, to deliver high-bandwidth wavelength services directly to end customers as infrastructure for the MPLS Ethernet and high-speed Internet backbone.&nbsp;&nbsp;Network-to-network interconnection points allow us to engage carrier partners to provide end to end service for carrier and enterprise customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We continue to invest in our fiber network to support the deployment of next-generation products and services, expand our addressable market and bring new customers on-net.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">In 2015, we completed several significant network enhancement and upgrade projects including the construction of a new MEF certified Carrier Ethernet MPLS/IP fiber overlay n</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">etwork designed to handle </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">FTTC</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> traffic within our network.&nbsp;&nbsp;This overlay network, totaling approximately 850 route miles, connects four key markets in our footprint (Pittsburgh, PA, Charleston, WV, Roanoke, VA and Ashburn, VA) and meets carrier class requirements for fast-rerouting, full redundancy and low latency performance.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">Our </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">second network operations center located in Pittsburgh, PA</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">, opened in 2014, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">is compatible with our FTTC all-IP network overlay.&nbsp;&nbsp;Now fully operational, the new network operations center provide</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> replication of all traditional functions of our existing network operations center located in Waynesboro, VA, including performance surveillance, repair, upgrade and maintenance of our fiber network and redundancy of our business continuity and disaster recovery functions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our parallel network operations centers provide technical surveillance of our network using industry leading network management systems.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

A mix of fiber optic and copper facilities connect our customers with the core network. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">The following summary does not describe all present and proposed federal and state legislation and regulations affecting the telecommunications industry.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some legislation and regulations are currently the subject of judicial proceedings, legislative hearings and administrative proposals which could change the manner in which this industry operates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Neither the outcome of any of these developments, nor their potential impact on us, can be predicted at this time.&nbsp;&nbsp;Regulation can change rapidly in the telecommunications industry, and such changes may have an adverse effect on us in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;See &#x201C;Risk Factors&#x201D; elsewhere in this report.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Regulation Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our communications services are subject to varying degrees of federal, state and local regulation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the federal Communications Act, the Federal Communications Commission (&#x201C;FCC&#x201D;) has jurisdiction over interstate and international common carrier services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the Telecommunications Act of 1996, the FCC has jurisdiction over certain aspects of local interconnection terms and rates between carriers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In addition to FCC regulation, our communications services are regulated to different degrees by state public service commissions and by local authorities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such local authorities have jurisdiction over public rights-of-way and video and telecommunications franchises. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our operations are subject to various federal and state laws intended to protect the privacy of customers who subscribe to our services.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FCC has regulations that place restrictions on the permissible uses that we can make of customer-specific information, known as </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">7</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#Table_of_Contents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Customer Proprietary Network Information (&#x201C;CPNI&#x201D;), received from subscribers and that govern procedures for release of such information and the Federal Trade Commission&#x2019;s &#x201C;Red Flag&#x201D; rules require that companies develop and implement written Identity Theft Prevention programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Federal Regulation of Interconnection and Interexchange Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Communications Act requires all common carriers to interconnect on a non-discriminatory basis with other carriers, imposes additional requirements on incumbent local exchange carriers (such as our RLEC&#x2019;s), and imposes even more comprehensive requirements on the largest ILECs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The large ILECs are required to provide competitors with physical collocation to allow competitors to place qualifying equipment in ILEC central offices; to unbundle some of their services into unbundled network elements (&#x201C;UNE&#x201D;) at &#x201C;forward looking&#x201D; rates, permit resale of some of their services, provide access to poles, ducts, conduits and rights-of-way, and to establish reciprocal compensation for the transport and termination of local traffic.&nbsp;&nbsp;The obligations of the large ILECs to provide these network facilities and services could be altered or removed by new legislation, regulations or court order.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">ILEC operating entities that serve fewer than 50,000 lines are defined as &#x201C;rural telephone companies&#x201D; under the Communications Act and are exempt from the additional requirements applicable to the large ILECs unless and until such exemption is removed by the state regulatory body.&nbsp;&nbsp;Each of our RLEC operations is considered separately and each has this rural telephone company exemption.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Intercarrier Compensation Reform</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Intercarrier compensation includes regulated interstate and intrastate access charges that we and other RLECs and CLECs receive from long distance carriers for the origination and termination of long distance calls and reciprocal compensation that interconnected local carriers pay to each other for terminating interconnected local wireline calls.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In 2011, the FCC released a significant order on intercarrier compensation reform.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the order, the FCC adopted a uniform national bill-and-keep framework (in which carriers do not collect or pay access charges or reciprocal compensation) as the ultimate end state for all telecommunications traffic exchanged between carriers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FCC established </font><font style="display: inline;">the </font><font style="display: inline;">$2 billion Connect America Fund (CAF) for RLECs and RLECs now receive support principally through the CAF rather than through intercarrier compensation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FCC order permitted ILECs to implement a new charge on end users to partially offset the loss in access charge revenues, the Access Recovery Charge (&#x201C;ARC&#x201D;), effective July 1, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The maximum ARC for residential customers is $3 per month after six years.&nbsp; Multi-line business customers have their Subscriber Line Charge and ARC combined capped at $12.20 per line.&nbsp;On May 23, 2014, the Tenth District Court of Appeals affirmed the FCC&#x2019;s order, including the establishment of the CAF and the reform of intrastate access and reciprocal compensation. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our RLECs began charging the ARC and began receiving funding from the CAF on July 1, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective July 1, 2013, our RLECs and CLECs took their rates for most intrastate access to interstate rates. Effective July 1, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and July 1, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, our RLECs and CLECS further reduced interstate and intrastate access charges as required by the FCC. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Net Neutrality.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">On March&nbsp;12, 2015, the FCC released an order re-classifying Internet service providers as common carriers under Title II of the Federal Communications Act and stating its intention to forbear from much of Title II regulation at this time. These new rules took effect on June&nbsp;12, 2015. At this early stage, it is uncertain what portions of Title II the FCC might apply and the FCC has not yet adjudicated any complaints under the new rules. Rules that increase the regulation of Internet services could limit our ability to efficiently manage our network and to respond to competitive challenges and could cause us to incur additional administrative costs. While it is uncertain what impact the new rules will have on </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">us</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">we do </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">not currently expect that the new rules will have a material adverse effect on </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">our </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">State Regulation of RLEC, CLEC and Interexchange Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Most states require wireline telecommunications providers to obtain authority from state regulatory commissions prior to offering common carrier services.&nbsp;&nbsp;State regulatory commissions generally regulate RLEC rates for intrastate services and RLECs must file tariffs setting forth the terms, conditions and prices for their intrastate services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our RLECs are subject to regulation in Virginia by the State Corporation Commission (&#x201C;SCC&#x201D;).&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We are certificated as a CLEC in Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Ohio and Kentucky.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although we file tariffs covering our CLEC services, our rates for such CLEC services generally fluctuate based on market conditions</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Local Government Authorizations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Certain governmental authorities require permits to open streets for construction and/or telecommunications franchises to install or expand facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Video franchises are also required for our video services.&nbsp;&nbsp;We obtain such permits and franchises as required.&nbsp;&nbsp;We hold video franchises in the City of Waynesboro, Botetourt County, City of Lynchburg, City of Staunton (for the Gypsy Hill Development only), Bedford County, Alleghany County, City of Covington, Town of Clifton Forge, and Town of Iron Gate.&nbsp;&nbsp;All of these localities are in the Commonwealth of Virginia.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We may be unable to successfully divest legacy businesses on a timely basis, which would hinder our strategy of accelerating our transformation to a pure play fiber bandwidth infrastructure company, and divestitures we do complete could adversely affect our </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">From time to time</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> we consider the divestiture of legacy businesses based on management's assessment of their strategic value to our business. Divesting</font><font style="display: inline;"> certain of our products or assets would be complex operationally due to their interrelationships with </font><font style="display: inline;">products </font><font style="display: inline;">and </font><font style="display: inline;">assets</font><font style="display: inline;"> we would desire to retain. Any divestiture also would have implications under our Credit Facility and 8% Notes. The inability to divest legacy businesses on a timely basis would hinder our strategy of accelerating our transformation to a pure play fiber bandwidth infrastructure company. Additionally, decisions to divest certain business operations could involve realization of losses, transition and wind-up expenses and the elimination of revenues along with associated costs, any of which could adversely affect our results of operations and cash flows, and may fail to yield the expected benefits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">may</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"> require additional capital to </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">fund our strategic growth plan</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">, and if we fail to </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">obtain this capital</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">, we may experience a material adverse effect on our business.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">O</font><font style="display: inline;">ur strategic growth plans </font><font style="display: inline;">require a significant amount of capital investment in fiber operations through organic and/or inorganic growth. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Additionally, t</font><font style="display: inline;">o remain competitive, we will need to </font><font style="display: inline;">continue to </font><font style="display: inline;">upgrade the technical requirements of our existing network infrastructure and build out our network with advanced fiber technology within our territories which will require a significant i</font><font style="display: inline;">nvestment of capital resources.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Additionally, the cost or extent of the work required for organic growth projects could be more significant than anticipated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any such unplanned capital expenditures may adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> expect that the cash we generate from operations combined with our cash on hand and marketable securities&nbsp;will be sufficient to satisfy our working capital requirements, capital expenditures and debt service requirements for the foreseeable future.&nbsp; Additionally, we have access to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">a revolving credit facility</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, which is currently undrawn. However,&nbsp;&nbsp;if our assumptions prove incorrect or if there are other factors that increase our need for additional liquidity, such as material unanticipated losses, loss of customers or a significant reduction in demand for our services or other factors, or if we are successful in obtaining additional major FTTC contracts or we make acquisitions, we would expect to seek additional sources of funds through refinancing or other means including additional equity financing.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is no assurance that we could obtain such additional financing on acceptable terms, if at all.&nbsp; If available, additional equity financing may dilute our stockholders and debt financing may restrict our ability to raise future capital.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We may not be able to complete acquisitions and acquisitions we do complete could result in operating difficulties, dilution and </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">other adverse consequences, which could adversely affect our results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We evaluate potential strategic transactions in order to pursue our strategy. At any given time, we may be engaged in discussions with respect to one or more of such transactions that may be material to our financial condition and results of operations. There can be no assurance that</font><font style="display: inline;"> any such discussions will result in the consummation of any transaction or that we will identify appropriate transactions on terms acceptable to us. Adverse capital markets and volatility in our stock price could also negatively impact our ability to make acquisitions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Future acquisitions may result in the dilutive issuances of equity securities, use of our cash resources and incurrence of debt or contingent liabilities. Acquisitions also may result in significant costs and expenses and charges to earnings, including those related to employee costs, integration costs, unexpected liabilities and legal, accounting and financial advisory fees. Any of these items could </font><font style="display: inline;">adversely affect our business, results of operations and cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We face substantial competition in our </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">markets; our competitors may have substantial business advantages over us and we may not be able to compete successfully.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We compete with ILECs, broadband service providers, incumbent cable operators, fiber companies and to a lesser extent, CLECs.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of the rapid growth in demand for broadband data, we expect that our competition will increase from market entrants offering FTTC, metro Ethernet solutions and other high-speed data services, including cable and wireless access. </font><font style="display: inline;"> Our competition includes </font><font style="display: inline;">ILECs, such as AT&amp;T, Verizon, Frontier, Windstream and Centurylink; national fiber service providers and CLECs, including Level 3 and Zayo, and national and regional cable operators, such as Comcast, Shentel, Cox, Time Warner Cable and Suddenlink.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">In addition, due to consolidation and strategic alliances within the telecommunications industry, we cannot predict the number of competitors that will emerge.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Such increased competition from existing and new entities could lead to price reductions, loss of customers, reduced operating margins and/or loss of market share.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Many of our competitors have financial resources, corporate backing, customer bases, marketing programs and brand names that are greater than ours.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, competitors may charge less than we do for services, causing us to reduce, or preventing us from raising, our fees.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Network delays or interruptions of service could cause us to lose customers.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">To be successful, </font><font style="display: inline;">we must provide our customers reliable network service.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of the risks to our network and infrastructure include:&nbsp;&nbsp;physical damage to outside plant facilities, power surges or outages; network equipment failures due to aging or other factors; software defects; human error; disruptions beyond our control, including disruptions caused by terrorist activities or severe weather; and failures in operational support systems.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Furthermore, as the demand for increased bandwidth from our customers has grown and as it continues to grow, our fiber optic network could experience greater data loads that may also result in network interruptions in service and reduced capacity for our customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Service interruptions and lack of redundancy could cause us to incur additional expenses and/or issue network outage credits to our customers and may cause us to lose customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">The telecommunications industry is generally characterized by rapid development and introduction of new technologies; if we are unable to adapt to these rapid changes, we could suffer price reductions, customer losses, reduced operating margins and/or loss of market share.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The telecommunications industry continues to experience rapid and significant changes in technologies and architectures to deliver new services to customers and to deliver existing services more cost-effectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect that new technologies will continue to enable advances in our customers&#x2019; environments that create new demand drivers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our future success will depend in part on our ability to anticipate and respond to the rapidly changing needs and demands of our customers on a timely basis and to compete with our competitors' offerings.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our failure to obtain and integrate new technologies and applications, and develop new service offerings to meet those customer needs or to keep pace with or exceed the service capabilities of our competitors could impact the breadth of our service portfolio, resulting in less competitive and compelling offerings that could impair our ability to attract and retain customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may be unable to keep pace with competitive offerings without making significant additional capital investments or adversely affecting our margins.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Revenue from certain of our more traditional products such as dedicated network services and certain voice services is growing slowly or is declining.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, our overall revenue growth is driven primarily by our Ethernet services and we must continue to develop those and other next generation services in order to continue to grow our revenue.&nbsp;&nbsp;New product development may be capital intensive and may pressure margins until the new products begin to generate substantial revenue.&nbsp;&nbsp;New products that are largely software based are increasingly complex and may require more customer support and additional systems development.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to investing in new technologies, we must replace equipment that supports our traditional services as that equipment ages or becomes redundant.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we do not properly manage this process, including the migration of customers to our newer technologies, we may lose customers and market share, and our margins and returns could be adversely affected.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">We need to obtain and maintain the necessary rights-of-way for our network from governmental and quasi-governmental entities and third parties, such as railroads, utilities, state highway authorities, local governments, transit authorities and private landowners.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Additionally, in many cases we require construction permits to complete fiber installations. </font><font style="display: inline;">We may not be successful in obtaining and maintaining these rights-of-way or </font><font style="display: inline;">construction permits or </font><font style="display: inline;">obtaining them on acceptable terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some agreements relating to rights-of-way may be short-term or revocable at will, and we cannot be certain that we will continue to have access to existing rights-of-way after the governing agreements are terminated or expire.&nbsp;&nbsp;If any of our right-of-way agreements were terminated or could not be renewed, we may be forced to remove our network facilities from the affected areas, relocate or abandon our networks.&nbsp;&nbsp;This would interrupt our operations and force us to find alternative rights-of-way and make unexpected capital expenditures.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">If we are unable to obtai</font><font style="display: inline;">n con</font><font style="display: inline;">struction permits in a timely manner, or at all, we could face delays</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">in fiber installations</font><font style="display: inline;">, incur unexpected cost for network redesign work,</font><font style="display: inline;"> or default on customer contracts. </font><font style="display: inline;">In addition, our failure to maintain the necessary rights-of-way, franchises, easements, licenses and permits may result in an event of default under our credit agreement and may subject us to legal complaints or claims.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;We may also incur costs resulting from a disruption of service or the relocation of equipment for other carriers that use our network under </font><font style="display: inline;">Indefeasible Rights to Use (&#x201C;IRU&#x201D;) arrangements</font><font style="display: inline;"> granted by us. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Under federal law, we have a right to use the poles,</font><font style="display: inline;"> ducts, and conduits </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of investor-owned utilities (electric and telephone) at regulated rates for our cables, including fiber optic facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of the poles we use are exempt from federal regulation because they are owned by utility cooperatives and municipal entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the </font><font style="display: inline;">rates, terms and conditions imposed by utilities are unreasonable, or if the utilities do not allow us access to the poles, ducts, and conduits in a timely manner, our b</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">usiness, financial results or financial condition could suffer. </font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Our rights to the use of fiber that are part of our network may be affected by the ability to continue long term contracts and the financial stability of our I</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">RU </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">fiber providers.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A portion of our services are provided on network fiber facilities licensed or leased from other network service providers through IRUs or similar arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The facilities under these agreements have remaining terms generally ranging from</font><font style="display: inline;"> less than</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">1</font><font style="display: inline;"> year to </font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;In these agreements, the network owner is responsible for network maintenance for which we pay such network owners.&nbsp;&nbsp;If our network provider under IRU agreements has financial troubles, it could adversely affect our costs, especially maintenance costs and ability to deliver service.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Also, if our network providers under IRU agreements are unable to obtain and maintain necessary rights-of-way and access to pole attachments for their fiber networks or if they fail to renew or extend our IRUs, our operations may be interrupted and/or we could incur material expenses </font><font style="display: inline;">if we were required to relocate </font><font style="display: inline;">to alternative network assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We are dependent upon interconnection agreements with other carriers to reach some of our customer locations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have interconnection agreements with </font><font style="display: inline;">I</font><font style="display: inline;">LEC</font><font style="display: inline;">s &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">in the</font><font style="display: inline;"> competitive</font><font style="display: inline;"> markets we serve.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on </font><font style="display: inline;">existing </font><font style="display: inline;">customer</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> and our assessment of growth opportunities in these markets, we purchase wholesale voice lines, data circuits and access to collocation facilities under these agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;From time to time, we are required to negotiate amendments to, extensions of, or replacements for these agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we may be required to negotiate new interconnection agreements in order to enter new markets in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may not be able to successfully negotiate amendments to existing agreements, negotiate new interconnection agreements, renew our existing interconnection agreements, opt in to new agreements or successfully arbitrate replacement agreements for interconnection on terms and conditions acceptable to us.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our inability to do so would adversely affect our existing operations and opportunities to expand our business in existing and new markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;If rates became unfavorable or we could no longer access collocation facilities, we could be forced to alter our service delivery which could reduce our customer base.&nbsp;&nbsp;As the FCC modifies and implements rules related to unbundling of ILEC network elements and collocation of competitive facilities at ILEC central offices, we generally have to renegotiate our interconnection agreements to implemen</font><font style="display: inline;">t those new or modified rules. </font>

			<a name="Market_for_Registrants_Common_Equity"></a><font style="display: inline;">Item 5.&nbsp;&nbsp;Market for Registrant&#x2019;s Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Market Information</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our common stock is traded on t</font><font style="display: inline;">he NASDAQ Global </font><font style="display: inline;">Market under the symbol &#x201C;LMOS.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;On </font><font style="display: inline;">March 4, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;">, the last reported sale price for our common stock was $1</font><font style="display: inline;">2.52</font><font style="display: inline;"> per share.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font><a name="MD_A"></a><font style="display: inline;">Item 7.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management&#x2019;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">You should read the following discussion of our financial condition in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the related notes included herein (Item 8).&nbsp;&nbsp;This discussion contains forward looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties.&nbsp;&nbsp;For additional information regarding some of these risks and uncertainties that affect our business and the industry in which we operate, please see &#x201C;Risk Factors&#x201D; and &#x201C;Forward-Looking Statements&#x201D; elsewhere in this report.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Lumos Network</font><font style="display: inline;"> Corp. (&#x201C;Lumos Networks,&#x201D; the &#x201C;Company,&#x201D; &#x201C;we,&#x201D; &#x201C;us,&#x201D; or &#x201C;our&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;"> is a fiber-based bandwidth infrastructure </font><font style="display: inline;">and service </font><font style="display: inline;">provider in the Mid-Atlantic region.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">We provide services to </font><font style="display: inline;">carrier</font><font style="display: inline;"> and enterprise customers, including</font><font style="display: inline;"> healthcare providers, local government agencies, financial institutions</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> educational institutions over our </font><font style="display: inline;">approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">8</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">00 route-mile fiber network.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our principal products and services include Multiprotocol Label Switching (&#x201C;MPLS&#x201D;) </font><font style="display: inline;">based</font><font style="display: inline;"> Ethernet, Metro Ethernet (&#x201C;Metro E&#x201D;), Fiber to the Cell</font><font style="display: inline;"> site</font><font style="display: inline;"> (&#x201C;FTTC&#x201D;) wireless backhaul and </font><font style="display: inline;">data</font><font style="display: inline;"> transport services, wavelength transport services and IP services. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our </font><font style="display: inline;">overall </font><font style="display: inline;">strategy is to transition into a pure-play fiber bandwidth infrastructure company through pursuit of expansion opportunities, both organic and inorganic. To achieve organic growth, our objective is to leverage and expand our fiber assets to capture the growing demand for data and mobility services among our carrier and enterprise customers in our marketplace. Our </font><font style="display: inline;">operating </font><font style="display: inline;">strategy is to (i) leverage our fiber network to expand to new fiber to the cell opportunities; (ii) monetize our approximately 8,600 route-mile fiber optic network by selling bandwidth infrastructure services to new and existing carrier and enterprise customers while maintaining a ratio of approximately 80% of our data revenue from on-net traffic;&nbsp; (iii) use our expansion and "edge-out&#x201D; strategies to expand into new markets and markets adjacent to our existing footprint to </font><font style="display: inline;">increase</font><font style="display: inline;"> our addressable market size; (iv) proactively manage our churn through several initiatives including upgrading existing customers from legacy technologies to carrier Ethernet services and continually improving network </font><font style="display: inline;">and operational performance;</font><font style="display: inline;"> (v) focus on managing resources from the declining legacy voice products into our faster growing and more profitable data products;</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> (vi) execute our success-based investment strategy to maintain our capital efficiency and expand margins. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Business Segments</font>
		</p>
