		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">technology to Ethernet products to improve efficiency.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">As we continue to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">implement our data growth strategy, which includes completing the extension of our fiber optic network in the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">key Virginia markets of Richmond and Norfolk, we believe that the effect of churn on legacy product lines will </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">continue to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">be more than offset by revenues from carrier Ethernet products, long-term FTTC contracts and new enterprise customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Our </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">R&amp;SB</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> segment provided </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">32.9%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">35.8%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">38.9%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> of revenue for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, respectively.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">This segment includes legacy voice and IP services products targeted at our residential and small business customers.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Revenue </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">declined </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">6.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> for </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">our </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">R&amp;SB</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">segment</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> as compared to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> primarily </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">due to the decline in revenues from legacy voice products. This decline is attributable to voice line loss resulting from residential wireless substitution, technology changes and product replacement by competitive voice service offerings from cable operators in our markets. We currently expect aggregate revenue from these businesses will continue to decline.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our RLEC access segment provided </font><font style="display: inline;">11.1%</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">11.3%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">10.9%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of revenue for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;This business requires limited incremental capital to maintain the underlying assets and delivers reasonably predictable cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, revenue decline over time is expe</font><font style="display: inline;">cted due to access line loss an</font><font style="display: inline;">d</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">regulatory actions taken to reduce intra-state tariffs by applicable regulatory authorities, </font><font style="display: inline;">principally the FCC and the SCC.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2011, the FCC released an order comprehensively reforming its Universal Service Fund (&#x201C;USF&#x201D;) and intercarrier compensation systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the order, the FCC determined that interstate and intrastate access charges, as well as local reciprocal compensation, should be eliminated entirely over time.&nbsp;&nbsp;These FCC pricing reductions commenced on July 1, 2012 and continue through July 1, 2020.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, a portion of the access revenue previously received from carriers is being recovered through payments from the FCC&#x2019;s &#x201C;Connect America Fund&#x201D; (&#x201C;CAF&#x201D;) and from increases in charges to end user subscribers in the form of rate increases and the FCC&#x2019;s &#x201C;Access Recovery Charge&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;These new payments and revenues were also effective July 1, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;These actions directly impact the access rates charged by our RLEC</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">, which provide service to the rural Virginia cities of Waynesboro and Covington, and portions of </font><font style="display: inline;">the Virginia c</font><font style="display: inline;">ounties of </font><font style="display: inline;">Alleghany, Augusta and Botetourt.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Our total revenues derived from cost recovery mechanisms, including the USF and the CAF, were </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;">1.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, $</font><font style="display: inline;">22.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">16.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively, </font><font style="display: inline;">most</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">of which are reported in our RLEC access segment.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

</font><font style="display: inline;">Our Adjusted EBITDA margins, as defined below, were </font><font style="display: inline;">45.0%</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">50.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">46.4%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Excluding the curtailment gain, our Adjusted EBITDA margin was 44.6% for 2014.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">O</font><font style="display: inline;">ur Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="display: inline;"> margin for 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">is </font><font style="display: inline;">essentially flat as compared to 2014 as the </font><font style="display: inline;">increase</font><font style="display: inline;"> in operating </font><font style="display: inline;">revenue</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and lower network access costs</font><font style="display: inline;"> we experienced</font><font style="display: inline;"> were offset by higher selling, general and administrative expenses</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Our operating income margins are also impacted by increased depreciation expense resulting from our capital investments in our fiber optic network an</font><font style="display: inline;">d internal business systems as well as restructuring charges incurred during the first quarter of 2015.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA, as defined by us, is net income attributable to Lumos Networks Corp. before interest, income taxes</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, depreciation and amortization and</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> accretion of asset retirement obligations, net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, other </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">(</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">income</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">) expenses, net, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">equity-based compensation, amortization of actuarial losses, employee separation charges, restructuring</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> charges </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and gain</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> (loss)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> on interest rate swap derivatives. Adjusted EBITDA margin is calculated as the ratio of Adjusted EBITDA, as defined above, to operating revenues.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial performance measure.&nbsp;&nbsp;It should not be considered in isolation, as an alternative to, or more meaningful than measures of financial performance determined in accordance with GAAP.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management believes that Adjusted EBITDA is a standard measure of operating performance and liquidity that is commonly reported in the telecommunications and high speed data transport industry and provides relevant and useful information to investors for comparing performance period to period and for comparing financial performance of similar companies.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Management utilizes Adjusted EBITDA internally to assess its ability to meet future capital expenditure and working capital requirements, to incur indebtedness if necessary, and to fund continued growth.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management also uses Adjusted EBITDA to evaluate the performance of its business for budget planning purposes and as factors in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">our </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">employee compensation programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Note 4 &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in Part II, Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Disclosures, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">provides a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">net income attributable to Lumos Networks Corp</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Operating revenues decreased $6.0 million, or 2.9%, from 2013 to 2014 resulting from a decrease in R&amp;SB segment revenues of $8.6 million, partially offset by an increase in data segment revenues of $2.5 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The growth in data segment revenues was primarily driven by an increase in FTTC revenue of $5.7 million, which increase was partially offset by declines in transport revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $8.6 million decline in R&amp;SB segment revenues is due primarily to line loss from legacy voice products. For further </font><font style="display: inline;">information </font><font style="display: inline;">regarding these revenue fluctuations, see &#x201C;Operating Revenues&#x201D; below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Operating income increased $4.6 million from $45.8 million in 2013 to $50.5 million in 2014 due primarily to the $10.8 million curtailment gain related to discontinuance of benefits under the postretirement medical plan referenced above, partially offset by a $4.5 million decrease in gross margin (operating revenues less network access costs) and a $2.9 million increase in depreciation and amortization costs due to capital investment primarily in our fiber network assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Variances in the individual line items on the consolidated statements of income are described in the operating expenses section below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Adjusted EBITDA was $100.6 million in 2014 compared to Adjusted EBITDA of $96.3 million in 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Excluding the curtailment gain for the postretirement medical plan, Adjusted EBITDA was $89.9 million for 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The year-over-year decrease in Adjusted EBITDA is primarily attributable to the decline in total operating revenues, as described above and in further detail below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Net income attributable to Lumos Networks increased $3.8 million from 2013 to 2014. Reflected in these results was a $4.6 million increase in operating income and decrease in other expenses due to the non-recurrence of secondary offering costs and costs associated with the debt refinancing in 2013, offset by an increase in interest expense of $0.7 million (net of changes in the fair value of interest rate swap derivatives) and increase in income tax expense of $2.4 million.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Selling, General and Administrative Expenses.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased $12.0 million, or 15.6%, in 2014 as compared to 2013 primarily as a result of a net curtailment gain of approximately $10.8 million recognized in 2014 due to the discontinuance of certain medical benefits under our postretirement medical plan and other reductions in personnel-related costs such as non-cash and incentive compensation and pension-related costs, partially offset by increased salaries and wages.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also incurred lower rent, repairs and maintenance and operating taxes, which decreases were partially offset by increased advertising and marketing costs and professional fees. </font><br /><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Depreciation and Amortization.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;Depreciation and amortization increased $2.9 million, or 6.8%, over 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;This net increase is attributable to a $3.5 million increase in depreciation expense, partially offset by a $0.6 million decrease in amortization expense related to customer intangibles for which an accelerated amortization method is applied based on these assets&#x2019; estimated pattern of benefits.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in depreciation expense is a result of the year-over-year increase in our depreciable base of assets primarily from capital investment in our network including infrastructure upgrades and fiber to the cell site installations and internal business systems.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Data.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Total operating expenses attributed to our data segment increased $4.3 million, or 8.5%, from 2013 to 2014 due to a $0.2 million increase in network access costs, a $2.2 million increase in network operating and engineering costs and a $1.9 million increase in other selling, general and administrative expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The increases in network access and operating costs are directly attributable to our investment of resources in our network </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">operations to support the growth in this segment in 2014 and drive future growth.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in selling, general and administrative costs is primarily attributable to the increase in allocated </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">corporate expenses as the data segment grows in relation to the other segments and the redirection of our sales, marketing, customer service, engineering and other resources to support and grow the data business.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Principles of Consolidation </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company, Lumos Networks Operating Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, and all of Lumos Networks Operating Company&#x2019;s wholly-owned subsidiaries and those limited liability corporations where Lumos Networks Operating Company or certain of its subsidiaries, as managing member, exercised control.&nbsp;&nbsp;All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated</font><font style="display: inline;"> in consolidation</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;"> recognize revenue </font><font style="display: inline;">when persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, services are rendered or products are delivered, installed and functional, as applicable, the price to the buyer is fixed and determinable and collectability is reasonably assured.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Certain services require payment in advance of service performance. </font><font style="display: inline;"> In such cases, </font><font style="display: inline;">we</font><font style="display: inline;"> record a service liability at the time of billing and subsequently recognize revenue ratably over the service period.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;"> bill customers certain transactional taxes on service revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;These transactional taxes are not included in reported revenues as they are recognized as liabilities at the time customers are billed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;"> earn revenue by providing </font><font style="display: inline;">services through </font><font style="display: inline;">access to and usage of </font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;"> network.&nbsp;&nbsp;Local service revenues are recognized as services are provided.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Carrier data</font><font style="display: inline;"> revenues are earned by providing switched access and other switched and dedicated services</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">to other carriers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues for equipment sales are re</font><font style="display: inline;">cognized at the point of sale.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Trade </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Accounts Receivable </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;"> sell</font><font style="display: inline;"> our</font><font style="display: inline;"> services to </font><font style="display: inline;">other communication carriers and to business and residential customers</font><font style="display: inline;"> primarily in Virginia</font><font style="display: inline;"> and West Virginia and portions</font><font style="display: inline;"> of Maryland, Pennsylvania, Ohio and Kentucky.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">We have</font><font style="display: inline;"> credit and collection policies to maximize collection of trade receivables and require deposits </font><font style="display: inline;">or prepayment of services </font><font style="display: inline;">on certain sales.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">estimate</font><font style="display: inline;"> an allowance for doubtful accounts based on</font><font style="display: inline;"> a review of specific customers with large receivable balances and for the remaining customer receivables use</font><font style="display: inline;"> historical results, current and expected trends and changes in credit policies.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> &nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Property, Plant and Equipment and Other Long-Lived Assets (Excluding Goodwill and Indefinite-Lived Intangible Assets)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Property, plant and equipment, finite-lived intangible assets and long-term deferred charges are recorded at cost and are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount should be evaluated pursuant to the subsequent measurement guidance described in Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201C;FASB&#x201D;) Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC&#x201D;) 360-10-35.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Impairment is determined by comparing the carrying value of these long-lived assets to management&#x2019;s best estimate of future undiscounted cash flows expected to result from the use of the assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the carrying value exceeds the estimated undiscounted cash flows, the excess of </font><font style="display: inline;">the asset&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;">carrying value over the estimated fair value</font><font style="display: inline;"> is recorded as an impairment charge</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We believe that no impairment indicators exist as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> that would require us to perform impairment testing for long-lived assets, including property, plant and equipment, long-term deferred charges and finite-lived intangible assets to be held and used.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Depreciation of property, plant and equipment is calculated on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful lives of the assets</font><font style="display: inline;">, which we review and update based on historical experiences and future expectations</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Buildings are depreciated over a 50-year life and leasehold improvements, which are categorized </font><font style="display: inline;">in</font><font style="display: inline;"> land and building</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">, are depreciated over the shorter of the estimated useful lives or the remaining lease terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;Network plant and equipment are </font><font style="display: inline;">generally </font><font style="display: inline;">depreciated over various lives from </font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">25</font><font style="display: inline;"> years</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Furniture, fixtures and other equipment are depreciated over various lives from </font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">24</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.</font><br /><font style="display: inline;"></font><br /><font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">Plant and equipment held under capital leases are amortized on a straight-line basis over the shorter of the lease term or estimated useful life of the asset.&nbsp;&nbsp;Amortization of assets held under capital leases, including certain software licenses, is included with depreciation expense.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Indefinite-Lived Intangible</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Goodwill and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">franchise rights </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">are considered to be</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> indefinite-lived intangible assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Indefinite-lived intangible assets are not subject to amortization but are instead tested for impairment annually or more frequently if an event indicates that the asset might be impaired.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">policy is to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">assess the recoverability of indefinite-lived assets annually on October 1 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">or more frequently if</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> adverse events or changes in circumstances indicate that impairment may have occurred.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We first consider whether to take a qualitative approach in determining whether it is more likely than not that a reporting unit&#x2019;s fair value is less than its carrying amount before applying the two-step quantitative goodwill impairment test promulgated by FASB ASC Topic 350.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we determine that it is more likely than not that a reporting unit&#x2019;s fair value is less than its carrying amount or if we elect to bypass the qualitative test for a specific period, the two-step process is used to test for goodwill impairment.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Step one requires a determination of the fair value of each of the reporting units and, to the extent that </font><font style="display: inline;">the</font><font style="display: inline;"> fair value of the reporting unit </font><font style="display: inline;">exceeds </font><font style="display: inline;">its carrying value (including goodwill), the step two calculation of implied fair value of goodwill is</font><font style="display: inline;"> not required and no impairment loss </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">Section</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> 412 and 430 of the Internal Revenue Code and ERISA Section</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> 302 and</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">303 establish minimum funding requirements for defined benefit pension</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">plans.&nbsp;&nbsp;The minimum required contribution is generally equal to t</font><font style="display: inline;">he target normal cost plus the shortfall amortization installments for the current plan year and each of the six preceding plan years less </font><font style="display: inline;">any calculated credit balance. </font><font style="display: inline;">Our</font><font style="display: inline;"> policy is to make contributions to stay at or above the threshold required in order to prevent benefit restrictions and related additional notice requirements and is intended to provide for benefits </font><font style="display: inline;">to be paid in the future</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">We are required to rec</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">ognize the overfunded or underfunded status of a defined benefit pension plan as an asset or liability in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">our</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> consolidated b</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">alance </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">heets and to recognize changes in that funded status in the year in which the changes occur through other comprehensive income (loss). </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">We are </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">required to measure plan assets and benefit obligations as of the date of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">our </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">fiscal year-end balance sheet and provide the required disclosures as of the end of each fiscal year. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Deferred income taxes are provided on an asset and liability method whereby deferred tax assets are recognized for deductible temporary differences and deferred tax liabilities are recognized for taxable temporary differences.&nbsp;&nbsp;Temporary differences are the differences between the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and their tax bases.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted for the effects of changes in tax laws and rates on the date of enactment. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">We recognize the effect of income tax positions only if those positions are more likely than not of being sustained.&nbsp;&nbsp;Recognized income tax positions are measured at the largest amount that is greater than 50% likely of being realized.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">We accrue interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in interest expense and income tax expense, respectively.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> For</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> balance sheet</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> presentation purposes</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> we net our</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> deferred</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> tax asset and liability positions by jurisdiction and present the net </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">deferred tax asset and/or liability </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">as non-current in accordance with </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">FASB Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">ASU</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> 2015-17 described in greater detail in Note 2 </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">in Part II, Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Equity</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">-based Compensation</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;"> account for share-based employee compensation plans under FASB ASC 718, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Stock Compensation</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Equity-based compensation expense from share-based equity awards is recorded with an offsetting increase to additional paid-in capital on the </font><font style="display: inline;">consolidated</font><font style="display: inline;"> balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;For equity awards with only service conditions, </font><font style="display: inline;">we</font><font style="display: inline;"> recognize compensation cost on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period for the entire award.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The fair value of common stock options granted </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">with service-only conditions</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">is</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> estimated at the respective measurement date using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model with assumptions related to risk-free interest rate, expected volatility, dividend yield and expected term.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;The fair value of restricted stock awards granted with service-only conditions is estimated based on the market value of the common stock on the date of grant reduced by the present value of expected dividends as applicable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain stock options and restricted shares granted by us contain vesting provisions that are conditional on achievement of a target market price for our common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The grant date fair value of these options and restricted shares </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">i</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">s adjusted to reflect the probability of the achievement of the market condition based on management&#x2019;s best estimate using a Monte Carlo</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> model</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;We initially recognize the related compensation cost for these awards that contain a market condition on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period as derived from the valuation model.&nbsp;&nbsp;We accelerate expense recognition if the market conditions are achieved prior to the end of the derived requisite service period.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the F</font><font style="display: inline;">inancial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201C;F</font><font style="display: inline;">ASB</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;"> issued </font><font style="display: inline;">Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">ASU</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2014-09, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">(&#x201C;ASU 2014-09&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;">, which will replace most existing revenue recognition guidance in U.S. GAAP when it becomes effective.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2014-09 requires an entity to recognize the amount of revenue to which it expects to be entitled for the transfer of promised goods or services to customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In August 2015, the FASB issued </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">ASU</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">2015-14, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606)</font><font style="display: inline;">, which defers the effective date of ASU 2014-09 for public business entities from annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2016, to annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Early application is permitted only as of annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2014-09 permits the use of either the retrospective or cumulative effect transition method.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">We have </font><font style="display: inline;">not yet selected a transition method and is still evaluating the effect that ASU 2014-09 will have on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In February 2015, the FASB issued ASU 2015-02, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Consolidation (Topic 820</font><font style="display: inline;">): </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Amendments to the Consolidation Analysis</font><font style="display: inline;"> (&#x201C;ASU 2015-02&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2015-02 provides a revised consolidation model for all reporting entities to use in evaluating whether they should consolidate certain legal entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;All legal entities will be subject to reevaluation under this revised consolidation model.&nbsp;&nbsp;The revised consolidation model, among other things, (i) modifies the evaluation of whether limited partnerships and similar legal entities are VIEs or voting interest entities, (ii) eliminates the presumption that a general partner should consolidate a limited partnership, and (iii) modifies the consolidation analysis of reporting entities that are involved with VIEs through fee arrangements and related party relationships.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2015-02 is effective for fiscal years, and interim reporting periods within those fiscal years, beginning after September 1, 2016.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">We do </font><font style="display: inline;">not expect the future adoption of ASU 2015-02 to have a material impact on </font><font style="display: inline;">our </font><font style="display: inline;">consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In the third quarter of 2015, </font><font style="display: inline;">we </font><font style="display: inline;">elected early adoption of F</font><font style="display: inline;">ASB ASU </font><font style="display: inline;">2015-03</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Simplifying the Presentation of Debt Issuance Costs </font><font style="display: inline;">(&#x201C;ASU 2015-03&#x201D;) and applied it retrospectively to all prior periods presented in the</font><font style="display: inline;"> consolidated</font><font style="display: inline;"> financial statements. The guidance simplifies the presentation of debt issuance costs by requiring debt issuance costs to be presented as a deduction from the corresponding liability, consistent with debt discounts. The recognition and measurement guidance for debt issuance costs is not affected. Therefore, these costs will continue to be amortized as interest expense over the life of the associated debt instrument.</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The adoption of ASU 2015-03 resulted in the presentation of $10.5 million of debt issuance costs as a reduction to long-term debt in the consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2015. </font><font style="display: inline;">We </font><font style="display: inline;">also reclassified $5.2 million of debt issuance costs from deferred charges and other assets to </font><font style="display: inline;">a reduction to </font><font style="display: inline;">long-term debt on the consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2014. The adoption of ASU </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">In the fourth quarter of 2015, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">we</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> elected early adoption of</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> FASB ASU No. 2015-17,&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes (Topic 740): Balance Sheet Classification of Deferred Taxes</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">&nbsp;(&#x201C;ASU 2015-17&#x201D;) and applied it retrospectively to all prior periods presented in the</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> consolidated</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> financial statements. ASU 2015-17 simplifies the presentation of deferred income taxes by requiring that deferred tax assets and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">deferred tax </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">liabilities be offset</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> by tax jurisdiction</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> and the</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> resulting</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> net deferred tax asset</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> and/or </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">net </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">deferred tax </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">liability amount be classified as noncurrent in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">the consolidated balance sheet</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">. The adoption of ASU 2015-17 resulted in the presentation of $2.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> million of deferred tax assets as a reduction </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">the noncurrent </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">net </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">deferred liability in the consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2015. We also </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">reclassified $5.6 million</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> of deferred tax assets from current assets to</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> a reduction to</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> the noncurrent </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">net </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">deferred tax liability as of December 31, 2014. </font><font style="display: inline;">The adoption of ASU 2015-07</font><font style="display: inline;"> did not impact net income or any other amounts previously reported on the consolidated statements of income or comprehensive income</font><font style="display: inline;"> or cash flows</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-02, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Leases (Topic 842) (</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;ASU 2016-02&#x201D;), which will replace most existing lease guidance in U.S. GAAP when it becomes effective.&nbsp; ASU 2016-02 requires an entity to recognize </font><font style="display: inline;color:#1F497D;">most</font><font style="display: inline;"> leases, including operating leases, on the consolidated balance sheet of the lessee. ASU 2016-02 is effective for public business entities for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2018, with early adoption permitted.&nbsp; ASU 2016-02 requires the use of a modified retrospective transition method with elective reliefs.&nbsp; We are still evaluating the effect that ASU 2016-02 will have on our consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<a name="Quantitative_and_Qualitative_Market_Risk"></a><font style="display: inline;">Item 7A.&nbsp;&nbsp;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We are exposed to market risks primarily related to </font><font style="display: inline;">interest rates on our variable</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">rate debt obligations</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;We </font><font style="display: inline;">entered into the $425 million Credit Facility </font><font style="display: inline;">in</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> and amended the Credit Facility to include Term Loan C for an additional $28 million on January 2, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;As of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">34</font><font style="display: inline;">8.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million was outstanding under our Credit Facility. </font><font style="display: inline;"> As of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, we had a leverage ratio of </font><font style="display: inline;">3.78</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00</font><font style="display: inline;"> and an interest coverage ratio </font><font style="display: inline;">6.7</font><font style="display: inline;">0</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00, both of which are </font><font style="display: inline;">in compliance with our debt</font><font style="display: inline;"> covenant requirement</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have other fixed rate, long-term debt in the form of </font><font style="display: inline;">unsecured notes and </font><font style="display: inline;">capital lease</font><font style="display: inline;"> obligations</font><font style="display: inline;"> totaling </font><font style="display: inline;">$150 million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;">.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively,</font><font style="display: inline;"> as of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the terms of our Credit Facility, we </font><font style="display: inline;">were</font><font style="display: inline;"> required to enter into interest rate derivative instruments for three years on 50% of our term loans</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;These interest rate agreemen</font><font style="display: inline;">ts expired on December 31, 2015, and did not replace or renew them, </font><font style="display: inline;">therefore we are</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">exposed to interest rate risk on the </font><font style="display: inline;">full amount of the term loan balances</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;We do not purchase or hold any financial derivative instruments for trading purposes. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, our financial assets in the </font><font style="display: inline;">consolidated</font><font style="display: inline;"> balance sheet included unrestricted cash </font><font style="display: inline;">and cash equivalents of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">13.</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, which is comprised of deposits in non-interest bearing accounts with financial institutions of $</font><font style="display: inline;">4.</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, highly liquid fixed income securities of $</font><font style="display: inline;">2.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> deposits in money market mutual funds of $</font><font style="display: inline;">6.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, and </font><font style="display: inline;">marketable securities of $</font><font style="display: inline;">88.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, substantially all of which are </font><font style="display: inline;">short-term </font><font style="display: inline;">fixed income securities</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other </font><font style="display: inline;">non-current </font><font style="display: inline;">securities and investments totaled $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.</font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million at December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, our cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were held in financial institutions, money market mutual funds, commercial paper and debt securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although we actively monitor the depository institutions and the performance and quality of our investments, we are exposed to risks resulting from deterioration in the financial condition or failure of financial institutions holding our cash deposits, decisions of our investment advisors and defaults in securities underlying the funds and investments.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">In accordance with our Board-approved investment policy we have instructed our investment management firm to </font><font style="display: inline;">prioritize </font><font style="display: inline;">liquidity and </font><font style="display: inline;">safety over investment return in choosing the investment vehicles for cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and </font><font style="display: inline;">they </font><font style="display: inline;">have diversified these investments to the extent practical in an effort to minimize our exposure to any one inve</font><font style="display: inline;">stment vehicle or financial institutions.</font>

Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Lumos Networks</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"> Corp.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 1.&nbsp;&nbsp;Organization</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Lumos Networks Corp. (&#x201C;Lumos Networks&#x201D; or the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) is a fiber-based bandwidth infrastructure and service provider in the Mid-Atlantic region with a network of long-haul fiber, metro Ethernet and Ethernet rings located primarily in Virginia and West Virginia, and portions of Maryland, Pennsylvania, Ohio and Kentucky.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company serves carrier, business and residential customers over its fiber network offering data, voice and IP services.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s principal products and services include Multiprotocol Label Switching (&#x201C;MPLS&#x201D;) based Ethernet, Metro Ethernet (&#x201C;Metro E&#x201D;), Fiber to the Cell (&#x201C;FTTC&#x201D;) wireless backhaul and fiber transport services, wavelength transport services, IP services and other voice services.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On October 14, 2011, NTELOS Holdings Corp. (&#x201C;NTELOS&#x201D;) announced a distribution date of October 31, 2011 for the spin-off of all of the then issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Lumos Networks, which operated NTELOS&#x2019;s wireline operations (the &#x201C;Business Separation&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to and in connection with the Business Separation, following the market close on October 31, 2011, NTELOS effectuated a 1-for-2 reverse stock split (the &#x201C;Reverse Stock Split&#x201D;) of its shares of Common Stock, $0.01 par value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The spin-off of Lumos Networks was in the form of a tax-free stock distribution to NTELOS stockholders of record as of the close of business on October 24, 2011, the record date (the &#x201C;Distribution&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;On October 31, 2011, NTELOS distributed one share of Lumos Networks common stock for every share of NTELOS&#x2019;s common stock outstanding, on a post-Reverse Stock Split basis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On November 20, 2013, in a secondary offering of the Company&#x2019;s common stock, Quadrangle Capital Partners LP. (&#x201C;Quadrangle&#x201D;) sold 2,888,939 shares, priced at $20.00 per share.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">On March 17, 2015, in an additional secondary offering of the Company&#x2019;s common stock, Quadrangle sold 1,600,000 shares on an underwritten basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 14, 2015, Quadrangle distributed its remaining 591,898 shares to its investors (the &#x201C;Distribution&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the shareholder agreement between Quadrangle and the Company expired as of the effective date of the Distribution.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company did not receive any proceeds from the offerings, and the Company&#x2019;s total shares outstanding did not change. All direct costs of these offerings, which were primarily legal, printing and accounting fees related to the preparation of the registration statement, which totaled $0.3 and $0.8 million, are included in other expenses in the consolidated statements of income for the year ended December 31, 2015 and 2013, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company did</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">n</font><font style="display: inline;">o</font><font style="display: inline;">t incur any direct costs related to offerings during the year ended December 31, 2014.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 2.&nbsp;&nbsp;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Principles of Consolidation and Basis of Presentation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company, Lumos Networks Operating Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, and all of Lumos Networks Operating Company&#x2019;s wholly-owned subsidiaries and those limited liability corporations where Lumos Networks Operating Company or certain of its subsidiaries, as managing member, exercised control.&nbsp;&nbsp;All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Accounting Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results could differ from those estimates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant items subject to such estimates and assumptions include the useful lives of fixed assets; the allowance for doubtful accounts; the valuation of deferred tax assets and/or liabilities, asset retirement obligations and equity-based compensation; goodwill impairment assessments; actuarial determination of employee benefi</font><font style="display: inline;">t obligations; stock warrants; and reserve for u</font><font style="display: inline;">ncertain income tax positions.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Changes in Accounting Principle</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company historically presented unamortized debt issuance costs, or fees directly related to issuing debt, as long-term assets on the consolidated balance sheets in accordance with existing GAAP. In the third quarter of 2015, the Company elected early adoption of Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201C;FASB&#x201D;) Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) 2015-03, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Simplifying the Presentation of Debt Issuance Costs </font><font style="display: inline;">(&#x201C;ASU 2015-03&#x201D;) and applied it retrospectively to all prior periods presented in the consolidated financial statements. The guidance simplifies the presentation of debt issuance costs by requiring debt issuance costs to be presented as a deduction from the corresponding liability, consistent with debt discounts. The recognition and measurement guidance for debt issuance costs is not affected. Therefore, these costs will continue to be amortized as interest expense over the life of the associated debt instrument.</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The adoption of ASU 2015-03 resulted in the presentation of $10.5 million of debt issuance costs as a reduction to long-term debt in the consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2015. The Company also reclassified $5.2 million of debt issuance costs from deferred charges and other assets to a reduction to long-term debt on the consolidated balance sheet as of </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">48</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2014. The adoption of ASU 2015-03 did not impact net income or any other amounts previously reported on the consolidated statements of income or comprehensive income or cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">The Company historicall</font><font style="display: inline;">y &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">classified </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);">its</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> deferred tax asset and/or deferred</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> tax</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> liability as either current or noncurrent on the consolidated balance sheets</font><font style="display: inline;"> in accordance with existing GAAP. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">In the fourth quarter of 2015, the Company elected early adoption of FASB ASU 2015-17,&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes (Topic 740): Balance Sheet Classification of Deferred Taxes</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">&nbsp;(&#x201C;ASU 2015-17&#x201D;) and applied it retrospectively to all prior periods presented in the financial statements. ASU 2015-17 simplifies the presentation of deferred income taxes by requiring that deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities be offset by tax jurisdiction and the resulting net deferred tax asset and/or net deferred tax liability amount be classified as noncurrent in the consolidated balance sheet. The adoption of ASU 2015-17 resulted in the presentation of $2.4 million of deferred tax assets as a reduction to the noncurrent deferred liability in the consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2015. The Company also reclassified $5.6 million of deferred tax assets from current assets to a reduction to the noncurrent net deferred tax liability as of December 31, 2014. </font><font style="display: inline;">The adoption of ASU 2015-07 did not impact net income or any other amounts previously reported on the consolidated statements of income or comprehensive income or cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes revenue when persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, services are rendered or products are delivered, installed and functional, as applicable, the price to the buyer is fixed and determinable and collectability is reasonably assured.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain services of the Company require payment in advance of service performance.&nbsp;&nbsp;In such cases, the Company records a service liability at the time of billing and subsequently recognizes revenue ratably over the service period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company bills customers certain transactional taxes on service revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;These transactional taxes are not included in reported revenues as they are recognized as liabilities at the time customers are billed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company earns revenue by providing services through access to and usage of its networks.&nbsp;&nbsp;Local service revenues are recognized as services are provided.&nbsp;&nbsp;Carrier data revenues are earned by providing switched access and other switched and dedicated services to other carriers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues for equipment sales are re</font><font style="display: inline;">cognized at the point of sale.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company considers its investments in all highly liquid debt instruments with an original maturity of three months or less, when purchased, to be cash equivalents.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s marketable securities at December 31, 2015 and 2014 consist of debt securities not classified as cash equivalents.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company classifies such debt securities as either held-to-maturity, when the Company has the positive intent and ability to hold the securities to maturity, or available-for-sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;Held-to-maturity debt securities are carried at amortized cost, adjusted for the amortization of premiums or accretion of discounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Available-for-sale securities are carried at fair value, with the unrealized gains and losses reported in other comprehensive income or loss, net of tax.&nbsp;&nbsp;All of the Company&#x2019;s debt securities not classified as cash equivalents were classified as available-for-sale securities as of December 31, 2015 and 2014.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company previously utilized a swingline credit facility that it had with its primary commercial bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;This swingline facility was terminated in April 2013, concurrent with the closing of the Company&#x2019;s debt refinancing (see Note 5).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company had a book overdraft related to this master cash account of $1.8 million as of December 31, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company classified the changes in the book overdraft amount in cash flows from operating activities on the consolidated statement of cash flows for the year ended December 31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Restricted Cash</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During 2010, the Company received a federal broadband stimulus award to bring broadband services and infrastructure to Alleghany County, Virginia.&nbsp;&nbsp;The total project was $16.1 million, of which 50% (approximately $8 million) was funded by a grant from the federal government.&nbsp;&nbsp;The project was completed as of December 31, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company was required to deposit 100% of its portion for the grant (approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;">8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million) into a pledged account in advance of any reimbursements, which was to be drawn down ratably following the grant reimbursement approvals which were contingent on adherence to the program requirements.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company received $3.8 million, $0.1 million and $1.0 million in the years ended December 31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, respectively, for the reimbursable portion of the qualified recoverable expenditures.&nbsp;&nbsp;T</font><font style="display: inline;">he Company has </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> remaining receivable for the reimbursable portion of the qualified recoverable expenditures as of December 31, 2015 and all amounts from the pledged account were released as of December 31, 2015. </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Property, Plant and Equipment and Other Long-Lived Assets (Excluding Goodwill and Indefinite-Lived Intangible Assets)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Property, plant and equipment, finite-lived intangible assets and long-term deferred charges are recorded at cost and are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount should be evaluated pursuant to the subsequent measurement guidance described in FASB</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC&#x201D;) 360-10-35.&nbsp;&nbsp;Impairment is determined by comparing the carrying value of these long-lived assets to management&#x2019;s best estimate of future undiscounted cash flows expected to result from the use of the assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the carrying value exceeds the estimated undiscounted cash flows, the excess of the asset&#x2019;s carrying value over the estimated fair value is recorded as an impairment charge.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company believes that no impairment indicators exist as of December 31, 2015 that would require it to perform impairment testing for long-lived assets, including property, plant and equipment, long-term deferred charges and finite-lived intangible assets to be held and used.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

No such costs were incurred during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 or 2014.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Amortization expense for the years ended December 31, 2015, 2014 and 2013 was $4.8 million, $9.2 million and $9.8 million, respectively.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Indefinite-Lived Intangible Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<br /><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Goodwill and franchise rights are considered to be indefinite-lived intangible assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Indefinite-lived intangible assets are not subject to amortization but are instead tested for impairment annually or more frequently if an event indicates that the asset might be impaired.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s policy is to assess the recoverability of indefinite-lived assets annually on October 1 and whenever adverse events or changes in circumstances indicate that impairment may have occurred.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company first considers whether to take a qualitative approach in determining whether it is more likely than not that a reporting unit&#x2019;s fair value is less than its carrying amount before applying the two-step quantitative goodwill impairment test promulgated by FASB ASC Topic 350.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the Company determines that it is more likely than not that a reporting unit&#x2019;s fair value is less than its carrying amount or if the Company elects to bypass the qualitative test for a specific period, the two-step process is used to test for goodwill impairment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Step one requires a determination of the fair value of each of the reporting units and, to the extent that the fair value of the reporting unit exceeds its carrying value (including goodwill), the step two calculation of implied fair value of goodwill is not required and no impairment loss is recognized.&nbsp;&nbsp;In testing for goodwill impairment, the Company utilizes a market approach that includes the use of comparable multiples of publicly traded companies whose services are comparable to ours and recent M&amp;A activity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
