		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of October 1, 2015, the Company performed its annual goodwill impairment test for each of its reporting units with goodwill, which are two of our three operating segments (data and R&amp;SB).&nbsp;&nbsp;After a preliminary assessment, the Company elected to bypass the qualitative assessment and applied step one of the quantitative test as described above. Based on the results of this annual impairment testing, the Company determined that the fair values of each of the data and R&amp;SB reporting units substantially exceed their respective carrying amounts and that no impairment exists. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The gross amount of goodwill was </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$133.7</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million and the accumulated impairment loss was </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$33.4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million for a net carrying amount of $100.3 million as of December 31, 2015 and 2014. There was </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">no</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> activity in the consolidated goodwill accounts for the years ended December 31, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2014 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Accounting for Asset Retirement Obligations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">An asset retirement obligation is evaluated and recorded as appropriate on assets for which the Company has a legal obligation to retire.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company records a liability for an asset retirement obligation and the associated asset retirement cost capitalized at the time the underlying asset is acquired.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to the initial measurement of the asset retirement obligation, the obligation is adjusted at the end of each period to reflect the passage of time and changes in the estimated future cash flows underlying the obligation.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">51</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#Table_of_Contents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">The Company enters into various facility collocation agreements and is subject to locality franchise ordinances.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company constructs assets at these locations and, in accordance with the terms of many of these agreements, the Company is obligated to restore the premises to their original condition at the conclusion of the agreements, generally at the demand of the other party to these agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognizes the fair value of a liability for an asset retirement obligation and capitalizes that cost as part of the cost basis of the related asset, depreciating it over the useful life of the related asset.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Included in certain of the franchise ordinances under which the Company&#x2019;s RLECs and CLECs operate are clauses that require the removal of the RLEC&#x2019;s and CLEC&#x2019;s equipment at the termination of the franchise agreement.&nbsp; The Company has not recognized an asset retirement obligation for these liabilities as the removal of the equipment is not estimable due to an indeterminable end date and the fact that the equipment is part of the public switched telephone network and it is not reasonable to assume the jurisdictions would require its removal.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Advertising Costs</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company expenses advertising costs and marketing production costs as incurred (included within selling, general and administrative expenses in the consolidated statements of income).&nbsp;&nbsp;Advertising expense for the years ended December 31, 2015, 2014 and 2013 was $0.7 million, $1.4 million and $0.8 million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Pension Benefits and Retirement Benefits Other Than Pensions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company sponsors a non-contributory defined benefit pension plan (&#x201C;Pension Plan&#x201D;) covering all employees who meet eligibility requirements and were employed prior to October 1, 2003.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pension benefits vest after five years of plan service and are based on years of service and an average of the five highest consecutive years of compensation subject to certain reductions if the employee retires before reaching age 65 and elects to receive the benefit prior to age 65.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company froze the Pension Plan effective December 31, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, no further benefits are being accrued by participants for services rendered beyond that date.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has a nonqualified pension plan that was also frozen as of December 31, 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Sections 412 and 430 of the Internal Revenue Code and ERISA Sections 302 and 303 establish minimum funding requirements for defined benefit pension plans.&nbsp;&nbsp;The minimum required contribution is generally equal to the target normal cost plus the shortfall amortization installments for the current plan year and each of the six preceding plan years less any calculated credit balance. The Company&#x2019;s policy is to make contributions to stay at or above the threshold required in order to prevent benefit restrictions and related additional notice requirements and is intended to provide for benefits to be paid in the future. The Company is required to rec</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">ognize the overfunded or underfunded status of a defined benefit pension plan as an asset or liability in its </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">c</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">onsolidated </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">b</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">alance </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">heets and to recognize changes in that funded status in the year in which the changes occur through other comprehensive income (loss). The Company is required to measure plan assets and benefit obligations as of the date of the Company&#x2019;s fiscal year-end balance sheet and provide the required disclosures as of the end of each fiscal year. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Consolas;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Consolas;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">The Company also provides certain life insurance benefits for retired employees that meet eligibility requirements through the postretirement welfare benefit plan (the &#x201C;Other Postretirement Benefit Plan&#x201D;), which is contributory.&nbsp;&nbsp;These obligations, along with all of the pension plans and other postretirement benefit plans, are assumed by the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;Eligibility for the life insurance plan is restricted to active pension participants age 50-64 as of January 5, 1994 and is not eligible to employees hired after April 1993.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company previously provided&nbsp;&nbsp;health care benefits for retired employees, however, the Company terminated those benefits effective December 31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Eligible retirees received partial compensation for settlement of accrued benefits through a series of supplemental pension payments in 2014. As a result, the Company recognized a curtailment gain of $10.8 million in the year ended December 31, 2014 (see Note 11)</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">The Company accounts for the pension and retirement benefits other than pensions by accruing the cost of such benefits over the service lives of employees. Unrecognized actuarial gains and losses are amortized over the estimated average remaining service period for active employees and over the estimated average remaining life for retirees. The Company recognizes in its consolidated balance sheets the amount of the Company&#x2019;s unfunded Accumulated Postretirement Benefit Obligation (&#x201C;APBO&#x201D;) at the end of the year. </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">Amounts recognized in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) are adjusted out of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) when they are subsequently recognized as components of net periodic benefit cost. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Consolas;font-size: 10pt">
			<br /><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">The Company sponsors a contributory defined contribution plan under Internal Revenue Code Section 401(k) for substantially all employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s policy is to match </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">100</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">% of each participant&#x2019;s annual contributions for contributions up to 1% of each participant&#x2019;s annual compensation and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">50</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">% of each participant&#x2019;s annual contributions up to an additional 5% of each participant&#x2019;s annual compensation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Company contributions vest after </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">two</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> years of service. </font><br /><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Operating Leases </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has operating leases for administrative office space and equipment, certain of which have renewal options.&nbsp;&nbsp;These leases, with few exceptions, provide for automatic renewal options and escalations that are either fixed or based on the consumer price index.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any rent abatements, along with rent escalations, are included in the computation of rent expense calculated on a straight-line basis over the lease term.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s minimum lease term for most leases includes the initial non-cancelable term and at least one renewal period to the extent that the exercise of the related renewal option or options is reasonably assured.&nbsp;&nbsp;A renewal option or options is determined to be reasonably assured if failure to renew the leases imposes an in-substance economic penalty on the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;Leasehold improvements are capitalized and depreciated over the shorter of the assets&#x2019; useful life or the lease term, including renewal option periods that are reasonably assured.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Deferred income taxes are provided on an asset and liability method whereby deferred tax assets are recognized for deductible temporary differences and deferred tax liabilities are recognized for taxable temporary differences.&nbsp;&nbsp;Temporary differences are the differences between the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and their tax bases.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted for the effects of changes in tax laws and rates on the date of enactment. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New (W1);"> The Company recognizes the effect of income tax positions only if those positions are more likely than not of being sustained.&nbsp;&nbsp;Recognized income tax positions are measured at the largest amount that is greater than 50% likely of being realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company accrues interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in interest expense and income tax expense, respectively. For balance sheet presentation purposes, the Company nets its deferred tax asset and deferred tax liability positions by tax jurisdiction and classifies the resulting net deferred tax asset and/or net deferred tax liability as noncurrent in accordance with ASU 2015-17.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Equity-based Compensation </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for share-based employee compensation plans under FASB ASC 718, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Stock Compensation</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Equity-based compensation expense from share-based equity awards is recorded with an offsetting increase to additional paid-in capital on the consolidated balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;For equity awards with only service conditions, the Company recognizes compensation cost on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period for the entire award.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The fair value of common stock options granted with service-only conditions is estimated at the respective measurement date using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model with assumptions related to risk-free interest rate, expected volatility, dividend yield and expected term.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of restricted stock awards granted with service-only conditions is estimated based on the market value of the common stock on the date of grant reduced by the present value of expected dividends as applicable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain stock options and restricted shares granted by the Company contain vesting provisions that are conditional on achievement of a target market price for the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The grant date fair value of these options and restricted shares was adjusted to reflect the probability of the achievement of the market condition based on management&#x2019;s best estimate using a Monte Carlo model (see Note 9).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company initially recognizes the related compensation cost for these awards that contain a market condition on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period as derived from the valuation model.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company accelerates expense recognition if the market conditions are achieved prior to the end of the derived requisite service period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Total equity-based compensation expense related to all of the share-based awards (Note 9), including the Company&#x2019;s 401(k) matching contributions, was $5.9 million, $4.3 million and $6.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, respectively, which amounts are included in selling, general and administrative expenses in the consolidated statements of income. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Future charges for equity-based compensation related to instruments outstanding at December 31, 2015 for the years 2016 through 2018 are estimated to be $4.0 million, $3.3 million, $1.0 million and less than </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million for each of </font><font style="display: inline;">2019</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 2020, respectively.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Fair Value Measurements</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Fair value is defined as the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;When determining the fair value measurements for assets and liabilities required to be recorded at fair value or for certain financial instruments for which disclosure of fair value is required, the Company uses fair value techniques that maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs to the extent possible.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, in situations where there is little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability at the measurement date, the fair value measurement reflects the Company&#x2019;s own judgments about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those judgments are developed by the Company based on the best information available in the circumstances, including expected cash flows and appropriately risk-adjusted discount rates, available observable and unobservable inputs. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">GAAP establishes a fair value hierarchy with three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair value:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;width: 100.00%;margin-left:0pt;">
			<tr>
				<td valign="top" style="width:07.66%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;height:1.00pt;padding:0pt 6.5pt">
					<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;height:1.00pt;overflow:hidden;font-size:0pt;">
						<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="top" style="width:92.34%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;height:1.00pt;padding:0pt 6.5pt">
					<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;height:1.00pt;overflow:hidden;font-size:0pt;">
						&nbsp;</p>
				</td>
			</tr>

				<td valign="top" style="border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;width:07.66%;height:10.80pt;padding:0pt 6.5pt">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
						<font style="display: inline;">&#x2022;</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="top" style="border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;width:92.34%;height:10.80pt;padding:0pt 6.5pt">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Level 1</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</font></p>
				</td>
			</tr>

				<td valign="top" style="border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;width:07.66%;height:22.05pt;padding:0pt 6.5pt">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
						<font style="display: inline;">&#x2022;</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="top" style="border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;width:92.34%;height:22.05pt;padding:0pt 6.5pt">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Level 2</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Unadjusted quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, or unadjusted quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are not active, or other inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability.</font></p>
				</td>

					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</table></div>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-09, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</font><font style="display: inline;">, which will replace most existing revenue recognition guidance in U.S. GAAP when it becomes effective.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2014-09 requires an entity to recognize the amount of revenue to which it expects to be entitled for the transfer of promised goods or services to customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In August 2015, the FASB issued </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">ASU</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">2015-14, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606)</font><font style="display: inline;">, which defers the effective date of ASU 2014-09 for public business entities from annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2016, to annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Early application is permitted only as of annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2014-09 permits the use of either the retrospective or cumulative effect transition method.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has not yet selected a transition method and is still evaluating the effect that ASU 2014-09 will have on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In February 2015, the FASB issued ASU 2015-02, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Consolidation (Topic 820</font><font style="display: inline;">): </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Amendments to the Consolidation Analysis</font><font style="display: inline;"> (&#x201C;ASU 2015-02&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2015-02 provides a revised consolidation model for all reporting entities to use in evaluating whether they should consolidate certain legal entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;All legal entities will be subject to reevaluation under this revised consolidation model.&nbsp;&nbsp;The revised consolidation model, among other things, (i) modifies the evaluation of whether limited partnerships and similar legal entities are VIEs or voting interest entities, (ii) eliminates the presumption that a general partner should consolidate a limited partnership, and (iii) modifies the consolidation analysis of reporting entities that are involved with VIEs through fee arrangements and related party relationships.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2015-02 is effective for fiscal years, and interim reporting periods within those fiscal years, beginning after September 1, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not expect the future adoption of ASU 2015-02 to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-02, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Leases (Topic 842) (</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;ASU 2016-02&#x201D;), which will replace most existing lease guidance in U.S. GAAP when it becomes effective.&nbsp; ASU 2016-02 requires an entity to recognize </font><font style="display: inline;color:#1F497D;">most</font><font style="display: inline;"> leases, including operating leases, on the consolidated balance sheet of the lessee. ASU 2016-02 is effective for public business entities for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2018, with early adoption permitted.&nbsp; ASU 2016-02 requires the use of a modified retrospective transition method with elective reliefs.&nbsp; The Company is still evaluating the effect that ASU 2016-02 will have on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Credit Facility</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On April 30, 2013, Lumos Networks Operating Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into a </font><font style="display: inline;">$425</font><font style="display: inline;"> million credit facility (the &#x201C;Credit Facility&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Credit Facility consists of a </font><font style="display: inline;">$100</font><font style="display: inline;"> million senior secured </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;">-year term loan (the &#x201C;Term Loan A&#x201D;), a </font><font style="display: inline;">$275</font><font style="display: inline;"> million senior secured </font><font style="display: inline;">six</font><font style="display: inline;">-year term loan (the &#x201C;Term Loan B&#x201D;); a </font><font style="display: inline;">$28</font><font style="display: inline;"> million senior secured incremental term loan facility under the existing credit facility (&#x201C;Term Loan C&#x201D;); and a </font><font style="display: inline;">$50</font><font style="display: inline;"> million senior secured </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;">-year revolving credit facility (the &#x201C;Revolver&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The proceeds from the Term Loan A and the Term Loan B were used to retire the prior credit facility outstanding amount of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$311</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and to pay closing costs and other expenses related to the transaction, with the remaining proceeds available for normal course capital expenditures and working capital purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2015, </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> borrowings were outstanding under the Revolver.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On January 2, 2015, the Company entered into the Term Loan C and amended certain terms of the Credit Facility.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company used the net proceeds from Term Loan C to fund new FTTC projects.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The amendment included changes to the maximum leverage ratio and the pricing of the Credit Facility as discussed below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On August 6, 2015, the Company prepaid </font><font style="display: inline;">$40.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of the outstanding principal of the Credit Facility, which was allocated ratably to Term Loans A, B and C.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company used proceeds from the issuance of the 8% Notes due 2022, discussed below, to fund these prepayments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Pricing of the amended Credit Facility is LIBOR plus </font><font style="display: inline;">3.00%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the Revolver and </font><font style="display: inline;">Term Loan A</font><font style="display: inline;"> and LIBOR plus </font><font style="display: inline;">3.25%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for Term Loan B and </font><font style="display: inline;">C</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Credit Facility does not require a minimum LIBOR rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Term Loan A matures in 2018 with quarterly payments of </font><font style="display: inline;">1.25%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum through December 31, 2016 and </font><font style="display: inline;">2.50%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum thereafter.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Term Loan B matures in 2019 with quarterly payments of </font><font style="display: inline;">1%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Term Loan C matures in 2019 with quarterly payments of </font><font style="display: inline;">1%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum beginning on June 30, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Revolver matures in full in 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Credit Facility is secured by a first priority pledge of substantially all property and assets of Lumos Networks Operating Company and all material subsidiaries, as guarantors, excluding the RLECs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The amended Credit Facility includes various restrictions and conditions, including a maximum leverage ratio of</font><font style="display: inline;"> 5.00</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00 through December 31, 2015, </font><font style="display: inline;">4.75:1.00 </font><font style="display: inline;">through December 31, 2016, </font><font style="display: inline;">4.50</font><font style="display: inline;">:</font><font style="display: inline;">1.00</font><font style="display: inline;"> through December 31, 2017, </font><font style="display: inline;">4.25:1.00 through December 31,</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2018 and </font><font style="display: inline;">4.00</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00 thereafter.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Credit Facility also sets a minimum interest rate coverage ratio of </font><font style="display: inline;">3.25</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2015, the Company&#x2019;s leverage ratio was </font><font style="display: inline;">3.78</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00 and its interest coverage ratio was </font><font style="display: inline;">6.70</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company was in compliance with its debt covenants as of December 31, 2015.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">Mandatory prepayments include an excess cash flow sweep equal to </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;"> of Excess Cash Flow, as defined under the Credit Agreement, for each fiscal year commencing in 2013 for so long as the leverage ratio exceeds </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">3.25</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:normal;">:1.00. Based on the excess cash flow calculation as of December 31, 2015, no mandatory prepayment was due for the year ended December 31, 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In accordance with the terms of the Credit Facility, the Company entered into interest rate swap agreements with a combined notional amount of 50 percent of the aggregate outstanding balance of Term Loan A and Term Loan B.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the interest rate swap agreements, the Company swapped one-month LIBOR with a fixed rate of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">0.5%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for certain agreements entered into in 2012 and </font><font style="display: inline;">0.8%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for certain agreements entered into in 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate swap agreements expired on December 31, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognized a net gain on interest rate swap derivatives of $0.7 and $0.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2015 and 2014, respectively, and a net loss of $0.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2013.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s effective interest rate on its Credit Facility for the year ended December 31, 2015 was </font><font style="display: inline;">3.96%</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">8% Notes due 2022</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On August 6, 2015, the Company issued $</font><font style="display: inline;">150</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in unsecured promissory notes (the &#x201C;8% Notes&#x201D;) to an affiliate of Pamplona Capital Management LLC (&#x201C;Pamplona&#x201D;). The net proceeds of the 8% Notes, after a $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million purchasers discount and payment of </font><font style="display: inline;">$7.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of closing costs, were used to prepay $40.0 million of the Company&#x2019;s existing Credit Facility with the remainder to be used for general corporate purposes, including to fund future growth opportunities. The 8% Notes bear interest at an annual fixed rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">8.00%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and mature on August 15, 2022.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest is payable in arrears on a quarterly basis on August 15, November 15, February 15, and May 15 of each year, beginning on November 15, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest is payable in cash or, at the election of the Company, through the issuance of additional notes or by adding the amount of the accrued interest to the unpaid principal amount of the 8% Notes outstanding at that time. The 8% Notes were also issued with </font><font style="display: inline;">5,500,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> warrants for no additional consideration to purchase shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock (the &#x201C;Warrants&#x201D;). The Company allocated the net proceeds received from the debt issuance to the 8% Notes and the equity-classified Warrants based on the relative fair value of the instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Company recognized a total discount on the 8% Notes of $</font><font style="display: inline;">24.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> of which $</font><font style="display: inline;">23.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million represents the value assigned to the</font><font style="display: inline;"> Warrants</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million represents the allocated portion of the aforementioned $1.5 million purchasers discount.&nbsp;&nbsp;The discount on the 8% Notes will be amortized to interest expense over the life of the debt using the effective interest method. See Note 9 for additional information regarding the valuation of the Warrants.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">In connection with the issuance of the 8% Notes in August 2015 and the Term Loan C financing in January 2015, the Company deferred an additional </font><font style="display: inline;">$6.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively, in debt issuance costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total unamortized debt issuance costs associated with the 8% Notes and Credit Facility are included in the table above, which amounts are </font><font style="display: inline;">presented </font><font style="display: inline;">as a reduction of long-term debt in the consolidated balance sheets in accordance with ASU 2015-03 (Note 2.) These costs are being amortized to interest expense over the life of the debt using the effective interest method.&nbsp;&nbsp;Amortization of debt issuance costs for the years ended December 31, 2015, 2014 and 2013 was </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s effective interest rate on the 8% Notes for the year ended December 31, 2015 was </font><font style="display: inline;">12.55%</font><font style="display: inline;">, which represents the contractual rate adjusted for the aforementioned discount and deferred debt issuance costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company receives patronage credits from CoBank and certain other of the Farm Credit System lending institutions (collectively referred to as &#x201C;patronage banks&#x201D;) which are not reflected in the interest rates above.&nbsp;&nbsp;The patronage banks hold a portion of the credit facility and are cooperative banks that are required to distribute their profits to their members.&nbsp;&nbsp;Patronage credits are calculated based on the patronage banks&#x2019; ownership percentage of the credit facility and are received by the Company as either a cash distribution or as equity in the patronage banks.&nbsp;&nbsp;The current patronage credit percentages are </font><font style="display: inline;">75%</font><font style="display: inline;"> in cash and </font><font style="display: inline;">25%</font><font style="display: inline;"> in equity.&nbsp;&nbsp;These credits are recorded in the consolidated statements of income as an offset to interest expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;The patronage credits were </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.</font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million for the years ended December 31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The aggregate maturities of the Term Loan A, Term Loan B and Term Loan C under the Credit Facility are </font><font style="display: inline;">$8.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in 2016, </font><font style="display: inline;">$13.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in 2017, </font><font style="display: inline;">$70.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in 2018 and </font><font style="display: inline;">$256.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;The revolver under the Credit Facility, under which no borrowings are outstanding as of December 31, 2015, matures in full in 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 8% Notes mature for $</font><font style="display: inline;">150.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in 2022.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Capital lease obligations </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In addition to the long-term debt discussed above, the Company has capital leases on vehicles with original lease terms of </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2015, the </font><font style="display: inline;">historical cost</font><font style="display: inline;"> and accumulated amortization of the related assets were </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2013, the Company entered into a financing arrangement with a provider of software services related to the upgrading of internal infrastructure, including certain software licenses, which the Company classified as a capital lease.&nbsp;&nbsp;The agreement extends through 2016 with payments due annually.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2015, the </font><font style="display: inline;">historical cost</font><font style="display: inline;"> and accumulated depreciation of the related asset were </font><font style="display: inline;">$5.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$3.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2015, the combined total net present value of the Company&#x2019;s future minimum lease payments is </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and the principal portion of these capital lease obligations was due as follows:&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in 2016, </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in 2017 and </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in 2018.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The fair value of commercial paper and corporate, municipal and U.S. government debt securities are provided by a third-party pricing service and are estimated using pricing models.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The underlying inputs to the pricing models are directly observable from active markets.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">However, the pricing models used do entail a certain amount of subjectivity and therefore differing judgments in how the underlying inputs are modeled could result in different estimates of fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">the Company </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">classif</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">ies</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> these fair value measurements as Level 2 within the fair value hierarchy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of interest rate </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">swap </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">derivatives </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">at December 31, 2015 </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">derived based on bid prices obtained from the administrative agents as of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">measurement</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;"> date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 8.&nbsp;&nbsp;Earnings per Share</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company computes basic earnings per share by dividing net income attributable to Lumos Networks Corp. applicable to common shares by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The impact on earnings per share of nonvested restricted shares outstanding that contain a non-forfeitable right to receive dividends on a one-to-one per share ratio to common shares is included in the computation of basic earnings per share pursuant to the two-class method.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company issues restricted shares from time to time with vesting terms that are based on achievement of certain stock price performance conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;These nonvested restricted shares are excluded from the computation of basic and diluted weighted average shares until the period in which the applicable performance or market conditions are attained.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company uses the treasury stock method to determine the number of potentially dilutive common shares from stock options and nonvested restricted shares during the period.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 9</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Stock </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Options, Restricted Stock and Stock Warrants</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Stock Options and Restricted Stock</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has an Equity and Cash Incentive Plan administered by the Compensation Committee of the Company&#x2019;s board of directors, which permits the grant of long-term incentives to employees and non-employee directors, including stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock awards, restricted stock units, incentive awards, other stock-based awards and dividend equivalents.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, t</font><font style="display: inline;">he maximum number of shares of common stock available for awards under the Equity and Cash Incentive Plan is </font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">00,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">1,</font><font style="display: inline;">1</font><font style="display: inline;">82,061</font><font style="display: inline;"> securities remained available for issuance under the Equity and Cash Incentive Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon the exercise of stock options or upon the grant of restricted stock under the Equity and Cash Incentive Plan, new common shares are issued or treasury stock is reissued.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company issued </font><font style="display: inline;">6,680</font><font style="display: inline;"> stock options and </font><font style="display: inline;">388</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">984</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of restricted stock under the Equity and Cash Incentive Plan during the year ended December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Options issued to employees with service-only conditions generally vest on a graded vesting schedule over a four to five year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Options generally cliff vest on the first anniversary of the grant date for n</font><font style="display: inline;">on-employee directors</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Restricted shares generally cliff vest on the third anniversary of the grant date for employees and generally cliff vest on the first anniversary of the grant date for non-employee directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some restricted stock awards vest on a graded vesting schedule over a five </font><font style="display: inline;">year period.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Certain stock options and restricted shares granted by the Company contain vesting provisions that are conditional on achievement of a target market price for the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2013, the Company recognized compensation expense totaling $1.8 million related to the accelerated vesting of equity awards for which the target market price had been achieved.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Dividend rights applicable to restricted stock with service-only vesting conditions are equivalent to the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;Restricted stock awards that vest based on achievement of a market condition are not eligible for dividends during the vesting period unless the Compensation Committee determines otherwise.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Stock options must be granted under the Equity</font><font style="display: inline;"> and Cash</font><font style="display: inline;"> Incentive Plan at not less than 100% of fair value on the date of grant and have a maximum life of ten years from the date of grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Options and other awards under the Equity</font><font style="display: inline;"> and Cash</font><font style="display: inline;"> Incentive Plan may be exercised in compliance with such requirements as determined by a committee of the board of directors.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Substantially all options outstanding were issued at a strike price equal to or greater than the fair value on the date of grant.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The fair value of each option award with service-only vesting conditions is estimated on the grant date using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">with assumptions related to risk-free interest rate, expected volatility, dividend yield and expected term</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">T</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">he risk-free rate is based on the zero-coupon U.S.&nbsp;Treasury rate in effect at the time of grant, with a term equal to the expected life of the options.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For awards granted in 2014</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and 2015</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Company use</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">d</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">historical trading prices for its common stock </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">to estimate volatility assumptions</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to 2014, the Company used peer group and other publicly available market data to estimate volatility assumptions due to limited trading history of its own common stock.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The expected option life represents the period of time that the options granted are expected to be outstanding</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and is determined using the simplified method</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected dividend yield is estimated based on the Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">actual</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> dividend yield at the date of the grant.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The weighted-average grant date fair value per share of stock options granted during the year</font><font style="display: inline;">s ended December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> was $</font><font style="display: inline;">8</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">09</font><font style="display: inline;">, $</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">68</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">.3</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The </font><font style="display: inline;">following weighted-average assumptions were used in estimating the grant date fair value of these awards:</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The accumulated benefit obligation for the defined benefit pension plan at December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> was $</font><font style="display: inline;">65</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">70.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The de</font><font style="display: inline;">crease in the projected benefit obligation is prima</font><font style="display: inline;">rily attributable to actuarial gains</font><font style="display: inline;"> resulting from a</font><font style="display: inline;">n in</font><font style="display: inline;">crease in the discount rate from </font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">85</font><font style="display: inline;">%&nbsp;&nbsp;at December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">4.20</font><font style="display: inline;">% at December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;"> and adjusted</font><font style="display: inline;"> mortality tables.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The accumulated benefit obligation represents the present value of pension benefits based on service and salary earned to date.&nbsp;&nbsp;The benefit obligation indicated in the table above is the projected benefit obligation which represents the present value of pension benefits taking into account projected future service and salary increases.&nbsp;&nbsp;The projected benefit obligation is equal to the accumulated benefit obligation as of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> since the Pension Plan was frozen effective as of December 31, 2012.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company reviews the assumptions noted in the above table annually or more frequently to reflect anticipated future changes in the underlying economic factors used to determine these assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The discount rates assumed reflect the rate at which the Company could invest in high quality corporate bonds in order to settle future obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;In doing so, the Company utilizes a Citigroup Pension Discount Curve applied against the Company&#x2019;s estimated defined benefit payments to derive a blended rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Citigroup Pension Discount Curve is </font><font style="display: inline;">derived from over 350 Aa corporate bonds</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also compares this to a Moody&#x2019;s ten year Aa bond index for reasonableness.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In developing the expected long-term rate of return assumption for the assets of the Pension Plan, the Company evaluated input from its third party pension plan asset managers, including their review of asset class return expectations and long-term inflation assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also considered the related historical ten-year average asset return at December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;"> as well as considering input from the Company&#x2019;s third party pension plan asset managers.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">It is the Company&#x2019;s policy to invest pension plan assets in a diversified portfolio consisting of an array of asset classes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The investment risk of the assets is limited by appropriate diversification both within and between asset classes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The assets are primarily invested in investment funds that invest in a broad mix of publicly traded equities, bonds and cash equivalents (and fair value is based on quoted market prices (Level 1 input within the fair value hierarchy previously defined)).&nbsp;&nbsp;The allocation between equity and bonds is reset quarterly to the target allocations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Updates to the allocation are considered in the normal course and changes may be made when appropriate.&nbsp;&nbsp;The bond holdings consist of three bond funds split relatively evenly between these funds at December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company believes that there are no material concentrations of risk within the portfolio of plan assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The assumed long term return noted above is the target long term return.&nbsp;&nbsp;Overall return, risk adjusted return, and management fees are assessed against a peer group and benchmark indices.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reporting on asset performance is provided quarterly and review meetings are held semi-annually.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to normal rebalancing to maintain an adequate cash reserve, projected cash flow needs of the plan are reviewed at least annually to ensure liquidity is properly managed.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Conclusion Regarding the Effectiveness of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Board of Directors and Stockholders</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Lumos Networks Corp.:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have audited Lumos Networks Corp.&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">, based on criteria established in</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework (</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). Lumos Networks Corp.&#x2019;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting (Item 9A). Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. Our audit also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#x2019;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. In addition, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In our opinion, Lumos Networks Corp. maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">, based on criteria established in </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework (</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated balance sheets of Lumos Networks Corp. and subsidiaries as of December&nbsp;31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, and the related conso</font><font style="display: inline;">lidated statements of income</font><font style="display: inline;">, comprehensive income, cash flows, and equity for each of the years in the three-year period ended December&nbsp;31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">, and our report dated March </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6 &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">expressed an unqualified opinion on those consolidated financial statements.</font>
